title: A finite subspace over a rational residue field has a basis with distinct orders
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], and let $R\subset K$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] containing $k$ and having fraction field $K$ (every element of $K$ is a quotient of two elements of $R$). Let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal and assume the quotient map restricts to an isomorphism $k\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak m$. Write $
u:K^	imes	o\mathbf Z$ for the normalized valuation: the quotient homomorphism $K^	imes	o K^	imes/R^	imes$ followed by the order-preserving identification of the value group with $\mathbf Z$, normalized so a generator of $\mathfrak m$ has value $1$. Let $U\subset K$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] of dimension $d$ [def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. Then $U$ has a $k$-basis $u_1,\ldots,u_d$ with $
u(u_1)<\cdots<
u(u_d)$. For $U=0$ this means the empty basis.

proof.text:
Induct on $d=\dim_k U$. If $d=0$, a basis has zero members by [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], so $U=0$ and its empty basis proves the assertion. Suppose $d>0$, and assume the assertion for every subspace of dimension less than $d$, with the same $k,K,R$. Choose a finite spanning family $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of $U$ using [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Write $e_i=a_i/b_i$ with $a_i,b_i\in R$ and $b_i
e0$, and put $q=\prod_i b_i
e0$. Then $qe_i=a_i\prod_{j
e i}b_j\in R$. Since $k\subset R$, every $x=\sum_i c_i e_i\in U$ satisfies $qx=\sum_i c_i(qe_i)\in R$.

proof.text:
For $x\in U\setminus\{0\}$ we have $qx\in R\setminus\{0\}$, so [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-ring-characterization] gives $
u(qx)\ge0$. Multiplicativity in [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic] gives $
u(x)\ge-
u(q)$. Thus the nonempty set $\{
u(x):x\in U\setminus\{0\}\}\subset\mathbf Z$ is bounded below. Subtract its integer lower bound and apply the least-element principle for natural numbers. Choose $u\in U\setminus\{0\}$ attaining its least value $n$. For every nonzero $x\in U$, $
u(x/u)=
u(x)-
u(u)\ge0$, hence $x/u\in R$ by [lem-sc-dvr-nonnegative-valuation-in-ring]; this also holds for $x=0$.

proof.text:
Let $ho:R	o R/\mathfrak m$ be the quotient map, and let $\iota:k\xrightarrow{\sim}R/\mathfrak m$ be its restriction, an isomorphism by hypothesis. Define $\lambda:U	o k$ by $\lambda(x)=\iota^{-1}(ho(x/u))$. Division by the fixed $u$ is additive, and for $c\in k$, $ho(cx/u)=\iota(c)ho(x/u)$, so $\lambda$ is $k$-linear. Also $\lambda(u)=1$. Put $W=\{x\in U:\lambda(x)=0\}$. For nonzero $w\in W$, $w/u\in\mathfrak m$; it cannot be a unit, since an ideal containing a unit contains $1$. The quotient definition $K^	imes/R^	imes$ of $
u$ gives $
u(w/u)
e0$, while its nonnegativity follows from the choice of $n$. Hence $
u(w)>n$.

proof.text: The vectors $f_i=e_i-\lambda(e_i)u$ lie in $W$. If $w=\sum_i c_i e_i\in W$, then $\sum_i c_i\lambda(e_i)=\lambda(w)=0$, and consequently $w=\sum_i c_i f_i$. Thus $W$ is finite-dimensional by [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Since $\lambda(cu)=c$ for $c\in k$, its image is all of $k$. The singleton $(1)$ is a basis of $k$ over itself, so its dimension is $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] with $V=U$, target $k$, and map $\lambda$: $1+\dim_kW=d$, hence $\dim_kW=d-1<d$. Both vector spaces are finite-dimensional, as required by that node.

proof.text:
Apply the induction hypothesis to the subspace $W\subset K$. It gives a basis $w_1,\ldots,w_{d-1}$ with strictly increasing orders (empty when $d=1$). Step 3 gives $
u(u)<
u(w_1)$ when $W
e0$. Every $x\in U$ decomposes explicitly as $x=\lambda(x)u+(x-\lambda(x)u)$ with the second summand in $W$, so $u,w_1,\ldots,w_{d-1}$ spans $U$. In a relation $cu+\sum_i c_iw_i=0$, applying $\lambda$ gives $c=0$, and independence of the basis of $W$ gives all $c_i=0$. This is a basis of $d$ members with the required strict order, completing the induction.
